proposals.before: On the next day, court ranks were advanced one step nationwide, two for those engaged in the funeral, taxes and corvée were waived for a year, and every official from prefect upward received the noble title marquis within the passes.
proposals.after: On the bingzi day, court ranks were advanced one step nationwide, two for those engaged in the funeral, taxes and corvée were waived for a year, and every official from prefect upward received the noble title marquis within the passes.
proposals.reason: Chinese 丙子 is a named sexagenary day after 辛未, not the next calendar day.

proposals.before: Grand Commandant Yang Jun was appointed grand tutor to oversee state affairs at the young emperor’s side.
proposals.after: Grand Commandant Yang Jun was appointed grand tutor to oversee state affairs.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 輔政 does not describe a young emperor.

proposals.before: In the eighth month, Sima You, prince of Guangling, was named crown prince; He Shao became his grand preceptor, Wang Rong his grand tutor, and Yang Ji his grand guardian.
proposals.after: In autumn, on the renwu day of the eighth month, Sima Yu, prince of Guangling, was named crown prince; He Shao became his grand preceptor, Wang Rong his grand tutor, and Yang Ji his grand guardian.
proposals.reason: The personal name 遹 is Yu, not You, and the date omits 秋八月壬午.

proposals.before: With that the edict ended. A further edict forbade imperial clansmen and officials to visit the imperial tombs.
proposals.after: A further edict forbade imperial clansmen and officials to visit the imperial tombs.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 又詔 has no clause saying the previous edict ended.

proposals.before: Prince Xiong of Liang was shifted from the eastern to the western theater as area commander beyond the passes, while Ruan Tan was sent to pacify the east and oversee the armies of Qing and Xu.
proposals.after: Prince Rong of Liang was shifted from the eastern to the western theater as area commander beyond the passes, while Ruan Tan was sent to pacify the east and oversee the armies of Qing and Xu.
proposals.reason: 梁王肜 transcribes as Rong, not Xiong.

proposals.before: Preceptor to Prince You of Guangling, Liu Shi, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent; Minister of Works, Prince Tai of Longxi, recorded the affairs of the secretariat.
proposals.after: Preceptor to the Prince of Guangling, Liu Shi, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent; Minister of Works, Prince Tai of Longxi, recorded the affairs of the secretariat.
proposals.reason: 廣陵王師 names the office, not a personal name You.

proposals.before: A stone was said to have “sprouted” in Yifang ward inside the capital.
proposals.after: A stone was said to have “sprouted” in Yinian ward inside the capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宜年里 is Yinian ward; Yifang is a different place-name and is not in the source.

proposals.before: There was a stone that grew in Yifang Ward in the capital.
proposals.after: There was a stone that grew in Yinian Ward in the capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宜年里 is Yinian, not Yifang.

proposals.before: Prince Lun of Zhao was recalled from the western command to the capital post of general of chariots and cavalry, while Prince Xiong of Liang took his place as general-in-chief in the west with authority over Yong and Liang and a mandate to hold the Guanzhong frontier.
proposals.after: Prince Lun of Zhao was recalled from the western command to the capital post of general of chariots and cavalry, while Prince Rong of Liang took his place as general-in-chief in the west with authority over Yong and Liang and a mandate to hold the Guanzhong frontier.
proposals.reason: The prince is 梁王肜 (Rong), the same Liang prince as earlier in the chapter; Xiong is the wrong given name.

proposals.before: General-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Lun of Zhao, was summoned to be general of chariots and cavalry; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Prince Xiong of Liang, was made general-in-chief who conquers the west and area commander for military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces, garrisoning within the passes.
proposals.after: General-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Lun of Zhao, was summoned to be general of chariots and cavalry; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Prince Rong of Liang, was made general-in-chief who conquers the west and area commander for military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces, garrisoning within the passes.
proposals.reason: 梁王肜 is Rong, not Xiong.

proposals.before: Xiahou Jun and Zhou Chu were sent against Qi Wannian in the eleventh month while Prince Xiong of Liang held a supporting camp at Haozhi.
proposals.after: Xiahou Jun and Zhou Chu were sent against Qi Wannian in the eleventh month while Prince Rong of Liang held a supporting camp at Haozhi.
proposals.reason: 梁王肜 is Rong; Xiong is a mistranslation of the same prince.

proposals.before: In the eleventh month, on the bingzi day, General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun, General Who Establishes Might Zhou Chu, and others were dispatched to attack Wannian; Prince Xiong of Liang encamped at Haozhi.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month, on the bingzi day, General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun, General Who Establishes Might Zhou Chu, and others were dispatched to attack Wannian; Prince Rong of Liang encamped at Haozhi.
proposals.reason: 梁王肜 is Rong, not Xiong.

proposals.before: On the renxu day in the twelfth month Crown Prince Sima You was stripped of his title and imprisoned with his three sons in the Jinyong fortress, while his mother Lady Xie was put to death.
proposals.after: On the renxu day in the twelfth month Crown Prince Sima Yu was stripped of his title and imprisoned with his three sons in the Jinyong fortress, while his mother Lady Xie was put to death.

proposals.before: On the bingzi day the young imperial grandson Sima Zang (written 𧇃 in the text) died.
proposals.after: On the bingzi day the imperial grandson 𧇃 died.
proposals.reason: The same chapter later establishes 皇孫臧 as living in the fifth month; 𧇃 who died in the first month must not be translated as Sima Zang.

proposals.before: Prince Xiong of Liang was recalled from the western command to take charge of secretariat business.
proposals.after: Prince Rong of Liang, general-in-chief who conquers the west, was summoned to take charge of secretariat affairs.
proposals.reason: 肜 is Rong, not Xiong; 徵 is a summons, and 征西大將軍 is the office held.

proposals.before: At the Ju River Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
proposals.after: At the Ju River, Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English fuses the place Ju River with the personal name Zhao Xiang, obscuring that Zhao Xiang is a person.

proposals.before: On the xinyou day Wang Yu and Prince Cui of Huailing forced the palace gates, seized Sun Xiu and Prince Lun’s other confederates, and put them all to the sword.
proposals.after: On the xinyou day Wang Yu and Prince Cui of Huailing forced the palace gates, seized Lun’s confederates Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others, and put them all to the sword.

proposals.before: Minister Sima Cui framed the decisive plot; Wang Yu, general of the left guards, with the high ministers acting in concert, led their household troops into the palace and slew Sun Xiu together with his two sons.
proposals.after: Minister Cui framed the decisive plot; Wang Yu, general of the left guards, with the high ministers acting in concert, led their household troops into the palace and slew Sun Xiu together with his two sons.

proposals.before: Prince Xiong of Liang was named grand steward while retaining the ministry of education on the jimao day.
proposals.after: Prince Tong of Liang was named grand steward while retaining the ministry of education on the jimao day.
proposals.reason: 肜 is Tong, not Xiong; the idiomatic English mistranslates the given name.

proposals.before: That year, twelve commanderies and kingdoms drought; six locusts.
proposals.after: That year, twelve commanderies and kingdoms suffered drought; six had locusts.
proposals.reason: The literal English is ungrammatical and omits the verbs implied by 旱 and 蝗.

proposals.before: On the dingmao day Prince Yong memorialized that Prince Jiong was plotting usurpation; he and Princes Ying, Xin, and Xiao converged on Luoyang demanding that Jiong be dismissed and sent home.
proposals.after: On the dingmao day Prince Yong of Hejian memorialized that Prince Jiong of Qi was plotting usurpation; together with Prince Ying of Chengdu, Prince Xin of Xinye, and Prince Xiao of Fanyang he converged on Luoyang, demanding that Jiong be dismissed and sent home.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the territorial princely titles and fuses 成都王穎 as ‘Princes Ying’, obscuring that 穎 is a different person from Jiong’s son 英.

proposals.before: Sima Zhao, son of Prince Rui of Donglai, was installed as prince of Qi to replace the extirpated line.
proposals.after: Sima Zhao, son of Prince Rui of Donglai, was installed as prince of Qi.
proposals.reason: The clause ‘to replace the extirpated line’ is not in the Chinese and invents a motive.

proposals.before: Li Te’s son Li Xiong recovered Yi Province from Jin forces in the fourth month.
proposals.after: In the fourth month, Li Te’s son Li Xiong again occupied Yi Province.
proposals.reason: ‘From Jin forces’ is not in the Chinese; 復據 means he again occupied the province.

proposals.before: In the fifth month the Yiyang chieftain Zhang Chang rebelled, set up Qiu Shen of Qiuchen as a bogus Han emperor surnamed Liu with reign Shenfeng, overran towns, and killed Prefect Liu Bin, General Yang Yi, and Prince Xin of Xinye.
proposals.after: In the fifth month the Yiyang chieftain Zhang Chang rebelled, set up Qiu Shen of Shandu as a bogus Han emperor surnamed Liu with reign Shenfeng, overran towns, and killed Prefect Liu Bin, General Yang Yi, and Prince Xin of Xinye.
proposals.reason: 山都 is Shandu, not Qiuchen.

proposals.before: In the fifth month, Yiyang Man Zhang Chang raised troops in rebellion, taking Qiuchen man Qiu Shen as lord, changing the surname to Liu, false title Han, era inception Shenfeng; he broke commanderies and prefectures; Nanyang Prefect Liu Bin, General Who Pacifies the South Yang Yi, and General-in-chief Who Guards the South, Prince Xin of Xinye, together met harm and died.
proposals.after: In the fifth month, Yiyang Man Zhang Chang raised troops in rebellion, taking Shandu man Qiu Shen as lord, changing the surname to Liu, false title Han, era inception Shenfeng; he broke commanderies and prefectures; Nanyang Prefect Liu Bin, General Who Pacifies the South Yang Yi, and General-in-chief Who Guards the South, Prince Xin of Xinye, together met harm and died.
proposals.reason: 山都 is Shandu, not Qiuchen.

proposals.before: Feng Yun of Linhuai rose in support of Zhang Chang and marched from Fuling into Xu Province.
proposals.after: Feng Yun of Linhuai raised troops in response to him and marched from Fuling into Xu Province.
proposals.reason: Chinese 應之 continues from Shi Bing’s Yang campaign; the idiomatic English invents an explicit Zhang Chang object.

proposals.before: By the jisi day the imperial camp had withdrawn to the Xuanyang parade ground.
proposals.after: By the jisi day the imperial camp had withdrawn to the Xuanwu parade ground.

proposals.before: On the jisi day the emperor wheeled the army back to the Xuanyang drill ground.
proposals.after: On the jisi day the emperor wheeled the army back to the Xuanwu drill ground.

proposals.before: At dawn on the bingshen new moon Chen Zhen of the right guards tricked the whole bureaucracy into the hall and launched a coup against Prince Ying.

proposals.reason: The Chinese 以詔召 is summoning by edict, not a trick, and 勒兵討 is leading troops to attack, not an invented 'coup'.

proposals.before: Prince Ying’s compound already displayed the nine-summons regalia; the prince of Chenliu sent the full accoutrements of investiture, and on the following day the emperor entered Ye with complete state panoply, attended only by Prince Chi, Wang Rong, and Xun Fan.
proposals.after: Prince Ying’s compound already displayed the nine-bestowal regalia; the prince of Chenliu sent the full accoutrements of investiture, and on the following day the emperor entered Ye with complete state panoply, attended only by Prince Chi, Wang Rong, and Xun Fan.

proposals.before: An old farmer gave him a steamed fowl, which he gratefully accepted.
proposals.after: An old man presented a steamed chicken, which the emperor accepted.

proposals.before: At Xin’an a frostbit ride threw him from his horse; Gao Guang of the ministry of the household gave him a face-wrap and earned the emperor’s praise.

proposals.reason: 尚書 is a secretariat minister, not the ministry of the household; the Chinese also states the injured foot.

proposals.before: Gong Sifan and other officers of Prince Ying plundered the north, slew Li Zhi and Zhang Yan, and besieged Ye until Duke Mo’s general Zhao Xiang broke them.

proposals.before: On the gengyin new moon Gong Sifan killed Wang Jing and Feng Xiong.

proposals.before: On the gengyin new moon of the ninth month, Gong Sifan again killed Pingyuan Prefect Wang Jing and Qinghe Prefect Feng Xiong.
proposals.after: On the gengyin new moon of the ninth month, Gongshi Fan again killed Pingyuan Prefect Wang Jing and Qinghe Prefect Feng Xiong.
proposals.reason: 公師藩 should be romanized Gongshi Fan.
